per_claim.claim: Vaccines work by introducing an agent that resembles a disease-causing microorganism into the body.

judgments.passage_text: A vaccine is a biological preparation that provides active acquired immunity to a particular infectious disease. A vaccine typically contains an agent that resembles a disease-causing microorganism and is often made from weakened or killed forms of the microbe, its toxins, or one of its surface proteins. The agent stimulates the body's immune system to recognize the agent as a threat, destroy it, and to further recognize and destroy any of the microorganisms associated with that agent that it may encounter in the future. Vaccines can be prophylactic (to prevent or improve the effects of a future infection by a natural or 'wild' pathogen) or therapeutic.
judgments.evidence: A vaccine typically contains an agent that resembles a disease-causing microorganism and is often made from weakened or killed forms of the microbe, its toxins, or one of its surface proteins.
judgments.reason: L'evidenza afferma esplicitamente che un vaccino contiene un agente che assomiglia a un microrganismo patogeno, corrispondendo direttamente all'affermazione del claim.

per_claim.claim: Vaccines work by introducing an agent that resembles a disease-causing microorganism into the body.

judgments.passage_text: A vaccine is a biological preparation that provides active acquired immunity to a particular infectious disease. A vaccine typically contains an agent that resembles a disease-causing microorganism and is often made from weakened or killed forms of the microbe, its toxins, or one of its surface proteins. The agent stimulates the body's immune system to recognize the agent as a threat, destroy it, and to further recognize and destroy any of the microorganisms associated with that agent that it may encounter in the future. Vaccines can be prophylactic (to prevent or improve the effects of a future infection by a natural or 'wild' pathogen) or therapeutic.

Some vaccines, such as those for influenza, need to be administered annually because the pathogen changes rapidly.

per_claim.claim: Inflation is a general increase in the prices of goods and services across an economy.

judgments.passage_text: In economics, inflation is a general increase in the prices of goods and services in an economy. This is usually measured using the consumer price index (CPI). When the general price level rises, each unit of currency buys fewer goods and services; consequently, inflation corresponds to a reduction in the purchasing power of money. The opposite of inflation is deflation, a sustained decrease in the general price level of goods and services. The common measure of inflation is the inflation rate, the annualized percentage change in a general price index.
judgments.evidence: In economics, inflation is a general increase in the prices of goods and services in an economy.
judgments.reason: L'evidenza afferma la stessa definizione di inflazione come aumento generale dei prezzi di beni e servizi in un'economia, corrispondendo esattamente al claim.

per_claim.claim: The placebo effect is a phenomenon where patients experience measurable beneficial physiological or psychological improvements after receiving a treatment with no active therapeutic ingredients.

judgments.passage_text: A placebo is a substance or treatment which is designed to have no therapeutic value. Common placebos include inert tablets (like sugar pills), inert injections (like saline), sham surgery, and other procedures. In general, placebos affect how patients perceive their condition and promote the body's chemical self-regulation. The placebo effect refers to the phenomenon in which some patients show a measurable beneficial physiological or psychological response after receiving a placebo. This response is not due to any active pharmaceutical ingredient.

judgments.passage_text: Seawater, or salt water, is water from a sea or ocean. On average, seawater in the world's oceans has a salinity of approximately 3.5%, or 35 parts per thousand. This means that every kilogram of seawater contains approximately 35 grams of dissolved salts. The salinity of seawater is largely due to the accumulation of dissolved minerals, primarily sodium chloride. Other major constituents include magnesium, sulfate, calcium, and potassium. The salt content of the ocean has been building up over hundreds of millions of years.
judgments.evidence: The salt content of the ocean has been building up over hundreds of millions of years.

Hydrothermal vent systems on the ocean floor also release significant quantities of minerals into seawater, contributing to its salt content. Because water evaporates from the ocean but the dissolved salts remain behind, the salinity of the ocean increases over geological time.

per_claim.claim: Stock prices are determined by supply and demand.

It postulates that, holding all else equal, in a competitive market, the unit price for a particular good or other traded item such as labor or a financial instrument, will vary until it settles at a point where the quantity demanded (at the current price) will equal the quantity supplied (at the current price), resulting in an economic equilibrium for price and quantity transacted. This mechanism determines the price of traded goods, including stocks.

per_claim.claim: Aging is fundamentally driven by the accumulation of cellular changes over time.

judgments.passage_text: Ageing or aging (see spelling differences) is the process of becoming older. The term refers especially to humans, many other animals, and fungi, whereas for example bacteria, perennial plants and some simple animals are potentially biologically immortal. In the broader sense, ageing can refer to single cells within an organism which have ceased dividing (cellular senescence) or to the population of a species (population ageing). In humans, ageing represents the accumulation of changes in a human being over time, and can encompass physical, psychological, and social change. Reaction time, for example, may slow with age, while knowledge of world events and wisdom may expand. Ageing is among the greatest known risk factors for most human diseases.
judgments.evidence: In humans, ageing represents the accumulation of changes in a human being over time, and can encompass physical, psychological, and social change.
judgments.reason: L'evidenza parla di accumulo di cambiamenti generici (fisici, psicologici, sociali), non specificamente di cambiamenti cellulari come affermato nel claim.

judgments.passage_text: Cellular senescence is a phenomenon characterized by the cessation of cell division. In their experiments during the early 1960s, Leonard Hayflick and Paul Moorhead found that normal human fetal cells in culture would divide between 40 and 60 times before entering a phase in which they would cease to divide (now called the Hayflick limit). Beyond this limit, the cells enter senescence. Senescent cells do not die; instead they remain metabolically active and secrete various pro-inflammatory signals (the 'senescence-associated secretory phenotype' or SASP), which are thought to contribute to age-related diseases and tissue dysfunction.
judgments.evidence: Senescent cells do not die; instead they remain metabolically active and secrete various pro-inflammatory signals (the 'senescence-associated secretory phenotype' or SASP), which are thought to contribute to age-related diseases and tissue dysfunction.
judgments.reason: L'evidenza descrive le cellule senescenti come un cambiamento cellulare che si accumula nel tempo e contribuisce a malattie e disfunzioni legate all'età, supportando l'idea che l'invecchiamento sia guidato dall'accumulo di tali cambiamenti.

judgments.passage_text: A telomere is a region of repetitive nucleotide sequences associated with specialized proteins at the ends of linear chromosomes. Telomeres are a protective structure of eukaryotic chromosomes, preventing chromosome deterioration or fusion with neighboring chromosomes. Because of the end-replication problem, telomeres shorten with every round of DNA replication. When the telomere becomes too short, the cell can no longer divide and enters senescence or undergoes apoptosis. Shorter telomeres are associated with cellular aging and a number of age-related diseases. In 1984, Carol Greider and Elizabeth Blackburn discovered telomerase, an enzyme that can lengthen telomeres.
judgments.evidence: When the telomere becomes too short, the cell can no longer divide and enters senescence or undergoes apoptosis. Shorter telomeres are associated with cellular aging and a number of age-related diseases.
judgments.reason: L'evidenza descrive l'accorciamento dei telomeri come un cambiamento cellulare che porta alla senescenza o apoptosi, e lo associa all'invecchiamento cellulare e a malattie legate all'età, supportando l'idea che l'invecchiamento sia guidato dall'accumulo di cambiamenti cellulari nel tempo.

judgments.passage_text: Senolytics are a class of drugs that selectively clear senescent cells from the body. Animal studies have shown that clearing senescent cells can extend healthy lifespan, restore physical function, and reverse several age-related conditions. Clinical trials in humans are ongoing. Examples of senolytic compounds include dasatinib (a cancer drug) combined with quercetin (a plant flavonoid).

per_claim.claim: Caloric restriction involves reducing calorie intake by 20 to 40 percent while maintaining proper nutrition.

judgments.passage_text: Caloric restriction (CR) or calorie restriction is a dietary regimen that reduces calorie intake without incurring malnutrition or a reduction in essential nutrients. 'Optimal' caloric restriction means reducing calories by 20–40% while consuming enough protein, vitamins, and minerals. Studies show that caloric restriction can significantly extend the lifespan of many organisms, including yeast, worms, flies, fish, rodents, and monkeys. The mechanisms include reduced oxidative stress, improved metabolic efficiency, and activation of longevity-related pathways such as sirtuins. Whether it extends human lifespan is still under investigation.

Senescent cells accumulate during aging and contribute to inflammation and tissue dysfunction. The first senolytic drugs were identified in 2015 by researchers at the Mayo Clinic. Animal studies have shown that clearing senescent cells can extend healthy lifespan, restore physical function, and reverse several age-related conditions. Clinical trials in humans are ongoing. Examples of senolytic compounds include dasatinib (a cancer drug) combined with quercetin (a plant flavonoid).

per_claim.claim: Telomerase is an enzyme discovered in 1984.

judgments.passage_text: A telomere is a region of repetitive nucleotide sequences associated with specialized proteins at the ends of linear chromosomes. Telomeres are a protective structure of eukaryotic chromosomes, preventing chromosome deterioration or fusion with neighboring chromosomes. Because of the end-replication problem, telomeres shorten with every round of DNA replication. When the telomere becomes too short, the cell can no longer divide and enters senescence or undergoes apoptosis. Shorter telomeres are associated with cellular aging and a number of age-related diseases. In 1984, Carol Greider and Elizabeth Blackburn discovered telomerase, an enzyme that can lengthen telomeres.

per_claim.claim: Aging is fundamentally driven by the accumulation of cellular changes over time.

judgments.passage_text: Ageing or aging (see spelling differences) is the process of becoming older. The term refers especially to humans, many other animals, and fungi, whereas for example bacteria, perennial plants and some simple animals are potentially biologically immortal. In the broader sense, ageing can refer to single cells within an organism which have ceased dividing (cellular senescence) or to the population of a species (population ageing). In humans, ageing represents the accumulation of changes in a human being over time, and can encompass physical, psychological, and social change. Reaction time, for example, may slow with age, while knowledge of world events and wisdom may expand. Ageing is among the greatest known risk factors for most human diseases.
judgments.evidence: In humans, ageing represents the accumulation of changes in a human being over time, and can encompass physical, psychological, and social change.
judgments.reason: L'evidenza parla genericamente di 'accumulazione di cambiamenti' fisici, psicologici e sociali, ma non menziona specificamente i cambiamenti cellulari, che sono l'elemento chiave del claim.

per_claim.claim: Human cells can divide around 40 to 60 times before entering senescence.

judgments.passage_text: Cellular senescence is a phenomenon characterized by the cessation of cell division. In their experiments during the early 1960s, Leonard Hayflick and Paul Moorhead found that normal human fetal cells in culture would divide between 40 and 60 times before entering a phase in which they would cease to divide (now called the Hayflick limit). Beyond this limit, the cells enter senescence. Senescent cells do not die; instead they remain metabolically active and secrete various pro-inflammatory signals (the 'senescence-associated secretory phenotype' or SASP), which are thought to contribute to age-related diseases and tissue dysfunction.
judgments.evidence: Leonard Hayflick and Paul Moorhead found that normal human fetal cells in culture would divide between 40 and 60 times before entering a phase in which they would cease to divide (now called the Hayflick limit). Beyond this limit, the cells enter senescence.
judgments.reason: L'evidenza afferma che le cellule fetali umane normali in coltura si dividono tra 40 e 60 volte prima di entrare in senescenza, corrispondendo esattamente al claim.

per_claim.claim: Caloric restriction involves reducing calorie intake by 20 to 40 percent while maintaining proper nutrition.

judgments.passage_text: Caloric restriction (CR) or calorie restriction is a dietary regimen that reduces calorie intake without incurring malnutrition or a reduction in essential nutrients. 'Optimal' caloric restriction means reducing calories by 20–40% while consuming enough protein, vitamins, and minerals. Studies show that caloric restriction can significantly extend the lifespan of many organisms, including yeast, worms, flies, fish, rodents, and monkeys. The mechanisms include reduced oxidative stress, improved metabolic efficiency, and activation of longevity-related pathways such as sirtuins. Whether it extends human lifespan is still under investigation.
judgments.evidence: 'Optimal' caloric restriction means reducing calories by 20–40% while consuming enough protein, vitamins, and minerals.

per_claim.claim: Humans have different blood types because of inherited variations in genes that control which antigens appear on the surface of red blood cells.

judgments.passage_text: A blood type (also known as a blood group) is a classification of blood, based on the presence and absence of antibodies and inherited antigenic substances on the surface of red blood cells (RBCs). These antigens may be proteins, carbohydrates, glycoproteins, or glycolipids, depending on the blood group system. Some of these antigens are also present on the surface of other types of cells of various tissues. Several of these red blood cell surface antigens can stem from one allele (or an allele pair) and collectively form a blood group system. Blood types are inherited and represent contributions from both parents.
judgments.evidence: Blood types are inherited and represent contributions from both parents.
judgments.reason: L'evidenza afferma che i gruppi sanguigni sono ereditati e provengono da entrambi i genitori, il che supporta direttamente l'affermazione che le differenze nei gruppi sanguigni sono dovute a variazioni ereditarie.

judgments.passage_text: The ABO blood group system is a classification of human blood based on inherited differences (polymorphisms) in the ABO gene, which encodes a glycosyltransferase enzyme. Blood group A has A antigens on red blood cells with B antibodies in the serum. Blood group B has B antigens with A antibodies. Blood group AB has both A and B antigens but neither antibody. Blood group O has neither antigen but both A and B antibodies. Because type O blood lacks both A and B antigens, it can be given to patients of any blood type without triggering an immune reaction, making it the universal donor type for red blood cells.
judgments.evidence: The ABO blood group system is a classification of human blood based on inherited differences (polymorphisms) in the ABO gene, which encodes a glycosyltransferase enzyme.

per_claim.claim: Receiving incompatible blood can trigger a dangerous immune reaction.

judgments.passage_text: A hemolytic transfusion reaction is a serious complication of a blood transfusion in which red blood cells that were transfused are destroyed by the recipient's immune system. The most common cause is ABO incompatibility. When the recipient receives blood containing antigens that they do not have, their pre-existing antibodies attack the donor red blood cells, causing hemolysis (destruction of red blood cells). This can result in kidney failure, disseminated intravascular coagulation, shock, and death. Hemolytic transfusion reactions are largely prevented by careful blood typing and cross-matching before transfusion.

per_claim.claim: Pain serves as a biological warning system that protects from harm.

judgments.passage_text: Chronic pain, or chronic pain syndrome, is a form of pain that is defined as pain lasting longer than three to six months. Unlike acute pain, which serves as a biological warning signal of tissue damage, chronic pain persists beyond the expected period of healing and is generally considered to be a malfunction of the nervous system. It is a major cause of disability and loss of quality of life. Chronic pain conditions include fibromyalgia, chronic migraine, complex regional pain syndrome, and neuropathic pain. Treatment typically involves a combination of medications, physical therapy, and psychological support.

The transmission of genes to an organism's offspring is the basis of the inheritance of phenotypic trait. Each person receives one allele for each gene from each parent; the combined expression of these alleles determines the individual's phenotype.

per_claim.claim: Evolution works through natural selection.

judgments.passage_text: Natural selection is the differential survival and reproduction of individuals due to differences in phenotype. It is a key mechanism of evolution, the change in the heritable traits characteristic of a population over generations. Charles Darwin popularised the term 'natural selection', contrasting it with artificial selection, which in his view is intentional, whereas natural selection is not. Variation exists within all populations of organisms. This occurs partly because random mutations arise in the genome of an individual organism, and offspring can inherit such mutations. Throughout the lives of the individuals, their genomes interact with their environments to cause variations in traits.
